clue.text: They are openly intended to counter hot-headedness

definitions.text: They are openly intended to counter hot-headedness

parts.words: They are openly intended to counter hot-headedness
parts.note: hot-headedness is read literally as a head growing hot in the sun, and these things are carried openly (opened up) to shade it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot-headedness' looks like a temper; here it is a head heated by the sun, and 'openly' hints at an umbrella-like shade being opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Parasols are held over the head to keep off the sun's heat.

clue.text: She makes us insane, almost

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside another, here the little word us going within the trimmed word
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, then shortened
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman is driving everyone nearly mad.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'insane', which reads as madness; read it as two words, 'in sane', so 'in' is the container signal and 'almost' drops the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a woman's first name, so a female pronoun can stand for it.

clue.text: Figure of a horse in the middle of the day

indicators.note: in places the horse within the time of day, splitting that word open

parts.note: midday is noon
a nag is an old or poor horse

explanation.surface: A painting of a horse at noon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a picture or statue of the horse; it is the geometric figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A nine-sided polygon is a geometric shape.

clue.text: St John's-wort, makes emu chirpy

indicators.note: makes signals that the following letters are worked into something new, a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A garden plant that cheers up a large flightless bird.
explanation.walkthrough: EMU and CHIRPY together give nine letters which rearrange into the botanical name; 'chirpy' looks like the mood, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypericum is the botanical genus of the yellow-flowered herb known by that common name.

clue.text: Edward returns to eastern post-hating it

indicators.note: returns says the short name for Edward is read backwards

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
a post is a position or station, as in a military posting

explanation.surface: Edward goes back to a posting in the east, which he loathes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' turns the short name backwards. The dash makes 'post-hating' look like one word, but 'post' is a posting and 'hating' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Detestation is intense loathing, a noun matching the gerund.

clue.text: This side for Brighton

parts.note: Brighton, an English resort town on the south coast, has a seaside; the clue asks which word goes before 'side'

explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON is a seaside resort on England's south coast; 'this side' is read as the word that joins 'side' to make seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: The coastal water of a resort town is what gives it its seaside character.

clue.text: Witch-ridden hag ?.

explanation.surface: An old hag is ridden by a witch.
explanation.walkthrough: A witch rides a broom; the same old word is also a dialect insult for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A besom is a twig broom, the kind a witch flies on, and in northern dialect a term of abuse for a contemptible woman.

clue.text: Sort to make mischief if fired

explanation.surface: Some sort of trouble starts when it is set alight.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads a burning piece of wood as the root of 'firebrand', a mischief-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand is a make or kind of goods; a burning brand, a firebrand, is a troublemaker.

clue.text: Cub-mistress naked do you say?

parts.note: a lady in charge of cub scouts who is unclothed would be a 'she bare', which sounds like the mother of bear cubs

explanation.walkthrough: A Cub Scout leader is a cub-mistress; 'naked' gives 'bare', sounding like the animal, so a female bare/bear rearing cubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A female bear is the mother who looks after cubs.

clue.text: A niggard gets round exam to become something of a preacher

indicators.note: gets round places the stingy person around the examination word, enclosing it

parts.note: a niggard is a miser
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A tightwad passes his viva and turns preachy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets round' looks like evading the exam; it is the stingy man wrapping the spoken test.
explanation.definitionFit: A moraliser lectures others on right and wrong, much as a preacher does.

clue.text: The reverse of light on a' dark subject

definitions.text: The reverse of light on a' dark subject

parts.words: The reverse of light on a' dark subject
parts.note: swap the terms: a dark patch on a light (bright) subject, the sun

explanation.walkthrough: Turn the phrase round: not light on a dark subject but dark on a light one, a darker area on the sun's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark spot on the bright solar surface is cooler than its surroundings.

clue.text: No mercenary lover

explanation.surface: A lover who is not in it for the money.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense goes back to the Latin amator, a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-professional does it for no pay, and the word comes from the Latin for one who loves.

clue.text: But it doesn't run into the Black Sea

definitions.text: But it doesn't run into the Black Sea

parts.words: But it doesn't run into the Black Sea
parts.note: the Latin for black names a West African river, which flows into the Atlantic, not the Black Sea

explanation.walkthrough: The name means 'black' in Latin, so a 'black' river might seem to flow to the Black Sea; it reaches the Gulf of Guinea instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The great West African river takes its name from the Latin word for black.

clue.text: Veronica's good wish to the racing motorist ?

definitions.text: good wish to the racing motorist

explanation.surface: Veronica wishes a racing driver luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Veronica' looks like a woman's name; it is the botanical genus of a small blue wild flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is the genus name for that blue-flowered plant, and wishing a driver to go fast and safely is saying 'go fast, go safely'.

clue.text: Visited by those wishing to get places

definitions.text: Visited by those wishing to get places

parts.words: Visited by those wishing to get places
parts.note: 'get places' sounds like ambition, but means buying or renting houses

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get places' looks like 'succeed in life'; here places are homes to buy or rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Property dealers are who house-hunters call on to find homes.

clue.text: This friend, however affectionate, is kept at a distance

definitions.text: This friend, however affectionate, is kept at a distance

parts.words: This friend, however affectionate, is kept at a distance
parts.note: a friend known only by letter is always far off, however warm the correspondence

explanation.walkthrough: The word joins 'friend' to make a correspondent you write to but rarely meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen-friend is a correspondent known through letters.

clue.text: One fixing the rates-by leave of God ?

parts.note: pace, from Latin, means with the permission of
the Maker is God

explanation.surface: Someone sets local taxes, with God's permission.
explanation.walkthrough: PACE is the Latin-derived word used before a name to mean 'with due respect to'. 'Rates' looks like local taxes; it is the speed of running or heartbeats.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacesetter decides how fast a race is run; a heart device regulates its beat.

clue.text: But they don't operate along the Strand

definitions.text: But they don't operate along the Strand

parts.words: But they don't operate along the Strand
parts.note: the Strand is a London street; a strand is also a beach, where shore patrols do work

explanation.walkthrough: THE STRAND is a famous street in central London; with a small s a strand is a shore, which these watchmen patrol.
explanation.definitionFit: Shore-watch officers patrol the coast against smuggling and to help ships.

clue.text: Number one consumes about a pound — it isn't true

indicators.note: consumes means the first piece swallows the others, enclosing them

parts.note: unity is the number one
re means about, concerning
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: The top man eats around a pound; it's a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' looks like the boss or oneself; here it is the abstract noun for the number one, which 'consumes' (encloses) the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreality is the state of not being real, a falsehood.

clue.text: Dog-hanger must court animal in disguise

indicators.note: in disguise says the letters are changed in appearance, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who hangs dogs must woo a disguised beast.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'give a dog a bad name and hang him': a slanderer is the one who does it.
explanation.definitionFit: A slanderer gives someone a bad name, which by the proverb is enough to hang a dog.

clue.text: There's no reasoning 'with him

parts.note: a person beyond reasoning is literally one who has lost his reason, a madman

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for a stubborn man is read literally as someone without reason.
explanation.definitionFit: A madman has no power of rational thought.

clue.text: Just the thing to get men to the opera

definitions.text: Just the thing to get men to the opera

parts.words: Just the thing to get men to the opera
parts.note: put this vehicle with 'men' and you get the name of Bizet's opera about a gypsy

explanation.walkthrough: A vehicle seems a way to take men to the opera house; put the word before MEN and you have Bizet's opera Carmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor vehicle carries people to places, and joined to 'men' it spells the opera's title.

clue.text: Fancy finding him in a mixed race

indicators.note: in places the pronoun inside the jumbled letters
mixed means the letters of race are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Liking a man in a race of mixed heritage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' rearranges the letters of 'race' as CERA, and 'in' puts the pronoun inside after its first letter. 'Fancy' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a wild illusion or fantasy of the mind.

clue.text: It makes a person singularly obsessed

definitions.text: It makes a person singularly obsessed

parts.words: It makes a person singularly obsessed
parts.note: 'singularly' looks like 'remarkably' but means with one thing only

explanation.walkthrough: 'Singularly' seems to mean 'extremely'; here it is 'about a single thing'.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession with one idea alone is a mental fixation.

clue.text: Intends to have the wherewithal

explanation.surface: Plans to have the money needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To plan to do something is to purpose it; resources or funds are what one lives by.

clue.text: A mild expletive for the imitative

parts.note: pish is an old exclamation of mild annoyance

explanation.surface: A gentle curse used about copycats.
explanation.walkthrough: PISH is an old-fashioned exclamation of contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Copying behaviour is said to ape, like a monkey mimicking.

clue.text: A knotty technical problem

parts.note: 'knotty' looks like 'difficult' but is also literal: a kind of knot in rope, as well as a snag

explanation.walkthrough: The word is both a knot used by sailors and a snag that holds things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag or holdup is also the name of a seaman's knot.

clue.text: Big task perhaps to conceal T. Atkins and Co's troubles

definitions.text: to conceal T. Atkins and Co's troubles

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters might be something else, a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A big job to hide the worries of the army.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Atkins is the stock name for a British soldier, and the First World War song says 'Pack up your troubles in your old kit-bag'.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers' canvas holdalls are where the song tells them to pack up their worries.

clue.text: What's the odds, taking in one little drink ?

indicators.note: taking in means the odds abbreviation holds the numeral inside

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds in horse racing
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gambler asks about the odds while having a quick drink.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, the starting price in betting, wraps I.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mouthful of liquid is a taste of a drink.

clue.text: It's clear I've reverted to depression

indicators.note: reverted says the letters of the contraction are turned backwards

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
a dent is a hollow or depression

explanation.surface: Plainly I have slipped back into gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' looks like low mood; it is a hollow. 'Reverted' turns IVE into EVI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obvious is plain to see.

clue.text: They're barred to Servicemen-or are they?

definitions.text: They're barred to Servicemen-or are they?

parts.words: They're barred to Servicemen-or are they?
parts.note: frames made of bars hold things such as rifles for soldiers, so they are barred, yet servicemen use them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Barred to' looks like 'forbidden to'; these frames are made of bars, as in a rifle stand used by servicemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Frameworks with bars hold weapons or kit in barracks.

clue.text: Money to trifle with ?

parts.note: trifling money, small sums, kept for small expenses

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifle with' looks like toying; it is money for trifling, small expenses.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fund of cash covers minor office expenses.
